title: 579. The Irish War of Independence: Showdown in London (Part 4)

sentences.en: I have never seen David so excited as he was before de Valera arrived.
sentences.zh: 我从未见过大卫像德瓦莱拉到来之前那样兴奋。

sentences.en: He had a big map of the British Empire hung up on the wall in the cabinet room, with great blotches of red all over it.
sentences.zh: 他在内阁会议室的墙上挂了一张巨大的大英帝国地图，上面到处都是大片的红色。

sentences.en: This was to impress de Valera.
sentences.zh: 这是为了给德瓦莱拉留下深刻印象。

sentences.en: In fact, David says that the aim of these talks is to impress upon de Valera the greatness of the Empire and to get him to recognise it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，大卫说这些会谈的目的是让德瓦莱拉感受到帝国的伟大，并让他承认这一点。

sentences.en: And the king.
sentences.zh: 还有国王。

sentences.en: David said to de Valera,
sentences.zh: 大卫对德瓦莱拉说：

sentences.en: The British Empire is a sisterhood of nations, the greatest in the world.
sentences.zh: 大英帝国是一个国家姐妹会，是世界上最伟大的姐妹会。

sentences.en: Look at this table.
sentences.zh: 看看这张桌子。

sentences.en: There sits Africa, English and Burr.
sentences.zh: 那里坐着非洲，有英国人和布尔人。

sentences.en: There sits Canada, French, Scotch and English.
sentences.zh: 那里坐着加拿大，有法国人、苏格兰人和英国人。

sentences.en: There sits Australia, representing many races, even Maoris.
sentences.zh: 那里坐着澳大利亚，代表着许多种族，甚至还有毛利人。

sentences.en: There sits India.
sentences.zh: 那里坐着印度。

sentences.en: There sit the representatives of England, Scotland and Wales.
sentences.zh: 那里坐着英格兰、苏格兰和威尔士的代表。

sentences.en: All we ask you to do is to take your place in this sisterhood of free nations.
sentences.zh: 我们要求你做的，只是在这个自由国家的姐妹会中占据你的位置。

sentences.en: It is an invitation, Mr. de Valera.
sentences.zh: 这是一个邀请，德瓦莱拉先生。

sentences.en: We invite you here.
sentences.zh: 我们邀请你到这里来。

sentences.en: So that was the diary of Frances Stevenson, who was personal secretary to David Lloyd George, the Prime Minister of Britain.
sentences.zh: 以上就是弗朗西丝·史蒂文森的日记，她是英国首相大卫·劳合·乔治的私人秘书。

sentences.en: And it's her entry for the 14th of July, 1921.
sentences.zh: 这是她1921年7月14日的日记条目。

sentences.en: And Dominic, you wanted me to read that in a Cockney accent.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你刚才想让我用伦敦腔读那段话。

sentences.en: But Frances Stevenson went to school in Clapham.
sentences.zh: 但弗朗西丝·史蒂文森是在克拉珀姆上的学。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And as someone who lives in Brixton, I know that everyone in Clapham speaks like that.
sentences.zh: 作为一个住在布里克斯顿的人，我知道克拉珀姆的每个人都那样说话。

sentences.en: So yet again, my mastery of accent comes to the rescue.
sentences.zh: 所以，我那精湛的口音模仿能力又一次派上了用场。

sentences.en: Okay, very good.
sentences.zh: 好吧，非常好。

sentences.en: And she is describing there the first meeting between the chief minister of the British Empire and the self-declared, so-a-dise-en, president of the Irish Republic.
sentences.zh: 她在那儿描述的是大英帝国首席大臣与自封的——也就是所谓的——爱尔兰共和国总统之间的第一次会面。

sentences.en: And what I can't help noticing there is that even though she's been to a very good school in Clapham, she seems to think that Maoris live in Australia.
sentences.zh: 我忍不住注意到，尽管她曾在克拉珀姆的一所非常好的学校上学，但她似乎认为毛利人住在澳大利亚。

sentences.en: So what's going on there?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Yes, I saw that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也看到了。

sentences.en: Also, there sits Africa, English and Burr.
sentences.zh: 还有，那里坐着非洲，有英国人和布尔人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I saw there are other people in Africa, but no one remembers who they were.
sentences.zh: 我看到非洲还有其他人，但没人记得他们是谁。

sentences.en: Yeah, she must have mentioned the Zulus.
sentences.zh: 是啊，她肯定提到了祖鲁人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this meeting between Lloyd George and de Valera, is it a success?
sentences.zh: 那么，劳合·乔治和德瓦莱拉之间的这次会面成功吗？

sentences.en: I mean, does this go down well with de Valera, this rhetoric?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这种修辞在德瓦莱拉那里行得通吗？

sentences.en: It's not a tremendous success, and we'll come back to this meeting a little bit later.
sentences.zh: 算不上巨大的成功，我们稍后会回到这次会面。

sentences.en: Lloyd George afterwards said to Frances Stevenson that de Valera was, and I quote, the man with the most limited vocabulary he'd ever met.
sentences.zh: 劳合·乔治事后对弗朗西丝·史蒂文森说，德瓦莱拉是他见过词汇量最贫乏的人，引用他的原话。

sentences.en: So that's slightly ominous.
sentences.zh: 这听起来有点不祥。

sentences.en: Frances Stevenson, by the way, she wasn't just his personal secretary, Lloyd George.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，弗朗西丝·史蒂文森不仅仅是劳合·乔治的私人秘书。

sentences.en: Oh no.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然不是。

sentences.en: This is David Lloyd George we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的可是大卫·劳合·乔治。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: She had been his mistress for almost a decade, and she ended up marrying him after his wife died.
sentences.zh: 她做了他近十年的情妇，在他妻子去世后，她最终嫁给了他。

sentences.en: So that's classic David Lloyd George behavior, and there'll be a lot of him in this episode.
sentences.zh: 这很符合大卫·劳合·乔治的一贯作风，这一集里会有很多关于他的内容。

sentences.en: And Dominic, generally, David Lloyd George you view as a very bad man.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，总的来说，你把大卫·劳合·乔治视为一个非常糟糕的人。

sentences.en: You've repeatedly gone record as saying you don't like him, but I can't help looking at this episode.
sentences.zh: 你曾多次公开表示不喜欢他，但我忍不住关注这一集。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: There seems to be a sneaking degree of admiration for him.
sentences.zh: 你对他似乎有一种隐秘的钦佩。

sentences.en: Well, we shall see.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们走着瞧。

sentences.en: I've said he's a bad man, a morally bad man.
sentences.zh: 我说过他是个坏人，一个道德上的坏人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But listeners to this podcast since the beginning will know that quite a lot of morally bad men score quite highly, in my estimation.
sentences.zh: 但从一开始就收听这个播客的听众会知道，在我看来，很多道德上的坏人得分相当高。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So a bad man, but a good negotiator.
sentences.zh: 所以，是个坏人，但也是个好的谈判者。

sentences.en: Well, we will see.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们走着瞧。

sentences.en: So, Tom, we've returned, haven't we, from Ireland?
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，我们从爱尔兰回来了，对吧？

sentences.en: We were in Ireland for the last three episodes with a friend of the show, Paul Rouse.
sentences.zh: 在过去的三集里，我们和节目的朋友保罗·劳斯一起在爱尔兰。

sentences.en: And we got to the summer of 1921 with Paul, didn't we?
sentences.zh: 我们和保罗一起走到了1921年的夏天，不是吗？

sentences.en: So we've been through two and a half years of guerrilla warfare, and the British and the
sentences.zh: 我们经历了两年半的游击战，英国人和

sentences.en: Irish have agreed a truce.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰人已经达成了停火协议。

sentences.en: But excitingly, the real drama is only just beginning, because this episode is about one of the most gripping intrigues in modern political history.
sentences.zh: 但令人兴奋的是，真正的戏剧性才刚刚开始，因为这一集讲述的是现代政治史上最引人入胜的阴谋之一。

sentences.en: It's about the deal that created two entities on the island of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 它讲述的是在爱尔兰岛上创造两个实体的交易。

sentences.en: So on the one hand, you have a Protestant-dominated Northern Ireland, and you have a Catholic-dominated
sentences.zh: 一方面，你有一个以新教徒为主的北爱尔兰，另一方面，你有一个以天主教徒为主的

sentences.en: Irish free state, which eventually becomes the Republic of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰自由邦，它最终成为了爱尔兰共和国。

sentences.en: And this episode also has a tremendous cast of characters.
sentences.zh: 这一集还有极其强大的角色阵容。

sentences.en: Who's your favourite?
sentences.zh: 你最喜欢谁？

sentences.en: I think my favourite is the guy who was Churchill's great friend, who's the Swell, who likes oysters and champagne and got...
sentences.zh: 我想我最喜欢的是那个丘吉尔的好朋友，那个风度翩翩、喜欢牡蛎和香槟，并且……的人。

sentences.en: Lord Birkenhead.
sentences.zh: 伯肯黑德勋爵。

sentences.en: Yeah, Dr. Crippen's mistress off, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 是啊，他把克里彭医生的情妇给带走了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, F.E.
sentences.zh: 是啊，F.E.

sentences.en: Smith.
sentences.zh: 史密斯。

sentences.en: F.E.
sentences.zh: F.E.

sentences.en: Smith.
sentences.zh: 史密斯。

sentences.en: Dan Jackson's a great hero.
sentences.zh: 丹·杰克逊是个伟大的英雄。

sentences.en: He's a tremendous man.
sentences.zh: 他是个了不起的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, he'll play a big part.
sentences.zh: 是啊，他会扮演重要角色。

sentences.en: So this episode, you've got him, you've got de Valera, you've got Lloyd George, you've got Winston Churchill, you have Michael Collins, a galaxy of stars.
sentences.zh: 所以这一集里，有他，有德瓦莱拉，有劳合·乔治，有温斯顿·丘吉尔，还有迈克尔·柯林斯，简直是群星璀璨。

sentences.en: It's very exciting.
sentences.zh: 非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: It's like an ITV, light entertainment programme from the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 就像20世纪80年代的独立电视台轻娱乐节目一样。

sentences.en: But the guy who really dominates is not an Irishman or an Englishman, it's a Welshman.
sentences.zh: 但真正占据主导地位的人既不是爱尔兰人也不是英国人，而是一个威尔士人。

sentences.en: We don't have enough Welshmen on the rest of his history, so it's great to get them in.
sentences.zh: 我们在《历史的其余部分》中没有足够的威尔士人，所以能让他们参与进来真是太好了。

sentences.en: So this is really Lloyd George's story, and he's one of the great characters in British history.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是劳合·乔治的故事，他是英国历史上最伟大的人物之一。

sentences.en: So just to give people, especially our overseas listeners, a sense of him, he's from an evangelical family in North Wales.
sentences.zh: 为了让大家，特别是我们的海外听众，对他有个了解，他来自北威尔士的一个福音派家庭。

sentences.en: He did lose his faith, but he's very, very intensely shaped by this kind of intensely religious, non-conformist background.
sentences.zh: 他确实失去了信仰，但他深受这种强烈的宗教、非国教背景的影响。

sentences.en: Also an interesting thing, he was brought up speaking Welsh, not English.
sentences.zh: 还有一件有趣的事，他从小讲威尔士语，而不是英语。

sentences.en: And that's interesting, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because he's dealing here with a lot of Irish negotiators who are all frantically trying to learn Irish, but have English as their native tongue.
sentences.zh: 因为他在这里要面对许多爱尔兰谈判代表，他们都在拼命学习爱尔兰语，但母语却是英语。

sentences.en: No, you're absolutely right, Tom, and he will slightly tease the Irish negotiators about this.
sentences.zh: 不，你说得完全对，汤姆，他会稍微取笑一下爱尔兰谈判代表这一点。

sentences.en: And in fact, he'll speak in Welsh to one of his colleagues, as we'll discover, a great ally of his called Tom Jones.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他会用威尔士语和他的同事交谈，正如我们将要发现的那样，他的一位伟大的盟友叫汤姆·琼斯。

sentences.en: Which is magnificent, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这太棒了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: A Welsh character called Tom Jones.
sentences.zh: 一个叫汤姆·琼斯的威尔士角色。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So Lloyd George, his Welshness is massively important to him.
sentences.zh: 所以劳合·乔治，他的威尔士身份对他来说极其重要。

sentences.en: He joined the Liberal Party as a populist outsider.
sentences.zh: 他作为一名民粹主义的局外人加入了自由党。

sentences.en: He always sort of sees himself as an anti-establishment figure, even when he's Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 即使在担任首相时，他也总是把自己看作是一个反建制的人物。

sentences.en: And his career is a really extraordinary story.
sentences.zh: 他的职业生涯是一个非常非凡的故事。

sentences.en: So he's a rhetorically brilliant, this sort of aggressive oratory.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一位修辞大师，有着这种咄咄逼人的演说风格。

sentences.en: He becomes a progressive Chancellor of the Exchequer under Herbert Henry Asquith, one of the architects of the welfare state.
sentences.zh: 他在赫伯特·亨利·阿斯奎斯手下成为了一位进步的财政大臣，是福利国家的建筑师之一。

sentences.en: On the other hand, he's very corrupt.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，他非常腐败。

sentences.en: He's a massive womanizer, and he is totally and utterly untrustworthy.
sentences.zh: 他是个十足的好色之徒，而且完全不可信。

sentences.en: So in 1916, he had stabbed Asquith, his former patron, in the back with Conservative support to become Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 所以1916年，他在保守党的支持下，背刺了他以前的赞助人阿斯奎斯，从而成为了首相。

sentences.en: And by 1921, he is the acknowledged master of British politics.
sentences.zh: 到了1921年，他已是公认的英国政治大师。

sentences.en: He's leading a coalition which is totally dependent on the support of the Conservatives.
sentences.zh: 他领导的联合政府完全依赖于保守党的支持。

sentences.en: So if he ever loses that, he is out.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他失去了这种支持，他就完了。

sentences.en: And so effectively, this great radical, the godfather of the British welfare state, is now, I mean, Lord Beaverbrook said he was a Prime Minister without a party.
sentences.zh: 因此，这位伟大的激进派、英国福利国家的教父，现在实际上——比弗布鲁克勋爵说他是一个没有政党的首相。

sentences.en: Effectively, he's in danger of being engulfed by the Conservatives, his great ancestral enemies.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他正面临被他伟大的祖传敌人——保守党所吞噬的危险。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: It's a really unusual situation in British political history where you have somebody who is seen as so charismatic, so dominating, that he almost
sentences.zh: 这是英国政治史上一个非常不寻常的情况，你有一个被认为如此有魅力、如此占据主导地位的人，以至于他几乎

sentences.en: has started to float free from party politics and to lead this kind of national coalition
sentences.zh: 开始脱离政党政治，纯粹依靠他的个人魅力，而不是

sentences.en: government purely on the basis of his personality rather than, you know, policies or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 政策或其他任何东西来领导这种全国性的联合政府。

sentences.en: And so what's his take on Ireland?
sentences.zh: 那么他对爱尔兰有什么看法？

sentences.en: Well, two important points there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里有两点很重要。

sentences.en: One, his non-conformist background means that he absolutely
sentences.zh: 第一，他的非国教背景意味着他绝对

sentences.en: despises Catholicism.
sentences.zh: 鄙视天主教。

sentences.en: I hate a priest wherever I can find him, he once said to one of his
sentences.zh: 无论在哪里见到牧师，我都讨厌他，他曾经对他的一位

sentences.en: Welsh friends.
sentences.zh: 威尔士朋友这样说。

sentences.en: He has no time for potpourri at all.
sentences.zh: 他根本没时间理会那些繁文缛节。

sentences.en: And does the fact that he's from a Celtic background mean that he's more sympathetic to
sentences.zh: 那么他来自凯尔特背景，是否意味着他更同情

sentences.en: Irish dreams of home rule?
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰人的自治梦想？

sentences.en: No, counterintuitively, the opposite.
sentences.zh: 不，反直觉的是，恰恰相反。

sentences.en: So because he's a Celt and because his Welshness is so important to him, he just thinks, what's wrong with the Irish?
sentences.zh: 因为他是凯尔特人，而且他的威尔士身份对他如此重要，他只是想，爱尔兰人到底怎么了？

sentences.en: You see, he thinks Welshness is perfectly reconcilable with the ideal of Britain and British unity in the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 你看，他认为威尔士身份与英国和联合王国中英国统一的理想是完全可以调和的。

sentences.en: And if we, the Welsh, are happy with it, what's wrong with the Irish?
sentences.zh: 如果我们威尔士人对此感到满意，那爱尔兰人有什么问题？

sentences.en: Why are they so troublesome?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们这么麻烦？

sentences.en: Why are they so difficult?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们这么难搞？

sentences.en: Of course, you know, a lot of people listening to this podcast will say they have very different histories.
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道，收听这个播客的很多人会说他们有非常不同的历史。

sentences.en: But for Lloyd George, there is always a sense that he doesn't perhaps have the slight embarrassment that some English people have with the Irish.
sentences.zh: 但对劳合·乔治来说，他总有一种感觉，他可能不像某些英国人那样对爱尔兰人感到轻微的尴尬。

sentences.en: You know, he just thinks, come on, crack on, knuckle down, what are you whinging about?
sentences.zh: 你知道，他只是想，得了吧，努力工作，脚踏实地，你们在抱怨什么？

sentences.en: Which a lot of English people are less likely, I think, to do because they feel a bit embarrassed about the history, about the famine and all of that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 我认为很多英国人不太可能这样做，因为他们对历史、饥荒以及所有这些事情感到有点尴尬。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Now, another really important point, I think, sometimes overlooked in accounts of the treaty negotiations.
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为在条约谈判的叙述中，还有一点非常重要，有时被忽视了。

sentences.en: Imagine if you were Lloyd George in early 1921, you're running the British
sentences.zh: 想象一下，如果你是1921年初的劳合·乔治，你在管理大英

sentences.en: Empire.
sentences.zh: 帝国。

sentences.en: The world looks like it's in total chaos.
sentences.zh: 世界看起来一片混乱。

sentences.en: You've had revolution and civil war in Russia.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯发生了革命和内战。

sentences.en: Russia.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯。

sentences.en: You've got massive unemployment in Britain, indeed, across Europe.
sentences.zh: 英国，实际上整个欧洲，都有大规模的失业。

sentences.en: You've got war in the Eastern Mediterranean between Greece and Turkey.
sentences.zh: 希腊和土耳其在东地中海发生了战争。

sentences.en: You have anti-colonial uprisings in India and Egypt.
sentences.zh: 印度和埃及发生了反殖民起义。

sentences.en: And at home, you're under massive pressure.
sentences.zh: 在国内，你承受着巨大的压力。

sentences.en: Britain has come very close in 1921 to a general strike.
sentences.zh: 1921年，英国非常接近大罢工。

sentences.en: Within the Tory party, a lot of people are saying, come on, Lloyd George is really corrupt and horrible.
sentences.zh: 在保守党内部，很多人都在说，得了吧，劳合·乔治真的很腐败，很糟糕。

sentences.en: Let's get rid of him.
sentences.zh: 让我们除掉他。

sentences.en: And two of your closest allies, Winston Churchill and this guy, Lord Birkenhead, who you like.

sentences.en: Anyway, the talks drag on and quite soon the British say, look, we've run out of patience.
sentences.zh: 总之，谈判拖延了下去，很快英国人就说，听着，我们没耐心了。

sentences.en: So on Friday, the 21st of October, Lloyd George says, OK, enough.
sentences.zh: 所以10月21日星期五，劳合·乔治说，好了，够了。

sentences.en: I want answers on three things.
sentences.zh: 我要三件事的答案。

sentences.en: Allegiance to the crown.
sentences.zh: 对王室的效忠。

sentences.en: You have to still acknowledge the king.
sentences.zh: 你们必须承认国王。

sentences.en: You have to still be members of the empire.
sentences.zh: 你们必须仍然是大英帝国的成员。

sentences.en: And we want naval defence guarantees, i.e. we will basically be in charge of your security.
sentences.zh: 我们需要海军防御保证，也就是说，我们基本上要负责你们的安全。

sentences.en: And if you don't give us the answer by Monday, the talks are over and we're back to the war.
sentences.zh: 如果周一之前不给我们答复，谈判就结束，我们重回战争状态。

sentences.en: So the following Monday, at long last, the Irish team come up with a counteroffer.
sentences.zh: 于是接下来的周一，爱尔兰代表团终于拿出了反建议。

sentences.en: And this has been drafted by de Valera himself.
sentences.zh: 这是由德瓦莱拉本人起草的。

sentences.en: And this is an idea called external association.
sentences.zh: 这是一个被称为“外部联系”的想法。

sentences.en: So Ireland will be a neutral republic.
sentences.zh: 所以爱尔兰将成为一个中立的共和国。

sentences.en: They're still going with that.
sentences.zh: 他们还在坚持这个想法。

sentences.en: The British Empire won't be a member of the British Empire, but it'll be associated with it.
sentences.zh: 大英帝国，不会是大英帝国的成员，但会与之保持联系。

sentences.en: You've put in your notes, all very reminiscent of Brexit negotiations,
sentences.zh: 你在笔记里写道，这一切都让人想起英国脱欧谈判，

sentences.en: endless hair splitting about tiny constitutional details that matter enormously to quite small numbers of people.
sentences.zh: 在微小的宪法细节上没完没了地钻牛角尖，而这些细节对极少数人来说却至关重要。

sentences.en: I mean, that's exactly what it's like, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这完全就是那种感觉，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实是。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I don't think that the average person in Ireland is really excited about whether it's a dominion or external association or those things.
sentences.zh: 我不认为爱尔兰的普通民众真的会对它是自治领还是外部联系之类的东西感到兴奋。

sentences.en: But if you're a nationalist, and if you've fought, and if you've lost people in the war, you know, of course it matters.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是一个民族主义者，如果你参加过战斗，如果你在战争中失去了亲人，你知道，这当然很重要。

sentences.en: Just as if you were, you know, somebody who'd been in the Leave campaign in 2016, you know, you really care about the outcome of the Brexit talks.
sentences.zh: 就像如果你是2016年脱欧运动的支持者，你当然会非常关心脱欧谈判的结果一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: Lloyd George treats the idea of external association with utter contempt.
sentences.zh: 劳合·乔治对“外部联系”的想法嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: And actually, again, most historians think the British are never going to go for this.
sentences.zh: 事实上，大多数历史学家也认为英国人绝不会接受这一点。

sentences.en: There's an Irish historian called Bill Kassane.
sentences.zh: 有一位爱尔兰历史学家叫比尔·卡萨恩。

sentences.en: The British didn't win the First World War to contemplate humiliation in their own backyard.
sentences.zh: 英国人赢得第一次世界大战可不是为了在自家后院蒙受羞辱。

sentences.en: Again, the First World War comparison.
sentences.zh: 又是第一次世界大战的类比。

sentences.en: And what is more, what's really interesting and will surprise people, the other dominions will not accept it either.
sentences.zh: 而且，更有趣且会让人们感到惊讶的是，其他自治领也不会接受这一点。

sentences.en: So Canada and Australia, for example, have made it very clear to London, they expect Ireland to remain within the empire.
sentences.zh: 例如，加拿大和澳大利亚已经非常明确地向伦敦表示，他们希望爱尔兰留在帝国之内。

sentences.en: They will not be happy if the Irish go their own way as a neutral republic.
sentences.zh: 如果爱尔兰作为中立共和国走自己的路，他们是不会高兴的。

sentences.en: So, you know, the empire is so fragile.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，帝国是如此脆弱。

sentences.en: It's at its largest ever extent in the early 1920s.
sentences.zh: 它在1920年代初达到了有史以来的最大规模。

sentences.en: But it seems so delicately poised.
sentences.zh: 但它似乎处于一种极其微妙的平衡状态。

sentences.en: And Lloyd George is always thinking about this.
sentences.zh: 劳合·乔治一直在考虑这个问题。

sentences.en: Anyway, they have this meeting on the Monday.
sentences.zh: 总之，他们在周一开了个会。

sentences.en: And afterwards, Lloyd George says to Collins and Griffiths,
sentences.zh: 会后，劳合·乔治对柯林斯和格里菲斯说：

sentences.en: Could you two stay behind, please, for a private chat?
sentences.zh: 你们两位能留下来私下聊聊吗？

sentences.en: Now, if the Irish team had been more sensible, they would never have had private chats with Lloyd George.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果爱尔兰代表团更理智一些，他们绝不会与劳合·乔治进行私下交谈。

sentences.en: They would never have allowed themselves to be seduced into this.
sentences.zh: 他们绝不会让自己被诱导去做这种事。

sentences.en: Because what it does is it splinters their team.
sentences.zh: 因为这样做会分裂他们的团队。

sentences.en: And Lloyd George is brilliant in small meetings.
sentences.zh: 劳合·乔治在小型会议上表现得非常出色。

sentences.en: He's a manipulator.
sentences.zh: 他是个操纵高手。

sentences.en: He can play on people and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他很擅长玩弄人心之类的手段。

sentences.en: And as time goes on, he has more and more of these private chats.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，他进行了越来越多这样的私下交谈。

sentences.en: He identifies Griffith and Collins as the people that, you know, he likes and he can do business with.
sentences.zh: 他认定格里菲斯和柯林斯是他喜欢且可以共事的人。

sentences.en: And they both start to warm to the British, the one thing that you would never have expected.
sentences.zh: 他们两人都开始对英国人产生好感，这可是你绝对想不到的事。

sentences.en: So Griffith actually writes to de Valera at one point.
sentences.zh: 所以格里菲斯有一次甚至写信给德瓦莱拉。

sentences.en: And he says, you know, I think if we show a little bit more goodwill to the British, they'll give us a great deal.
sentences.zh: 他说，我认为如果我们对英国人表现出多一点善意，他们会给我们很大的让步。

sentences.en: Which you would think, that's mad.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得，这简直疯了。

sentences.en: You've just drunk the British Kool-Aid.
sentences.zh: 你简直是被英国人的迷魂汤灌醉了。

sentences.en: The really remarkable thing is that Collins, the IRA's head of intelligence, he also starts to warm to the British.
sentences.zh: 真正引人注目的是，爱尔兰共和军的情报主管柯林斯，也开始对英国人产生好感。

sentences.en: And you know the person he really likes gets somewhere with?
sentences.zh: 你知道他真正喜欢并能与之达成共识的人是谁吗？

sentences.en: Lord Birkenhead.
sentences.zh: 伯肯黑德勋爵。

sentences.en: F.E.
sentences.zh: F.E.

sentences.en: Smith.
sentences.zh: 史密斯。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是他。

sentences.en: He thinks, because they're men's men, they're alpha males, they like bullying people, they like drinking, they like eating oysters or whatever.
sentences.zh: 他觉得，因为他们都是硬汉，都是雄性领袖，喜欢欺负人，喜欢喝酒，喜欢吃牡蛎之类的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They like bants.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢开玩笑。

sentences.en: And actually, Collins starts getting to the meetings a little bit early so they can have a bit of banter with Lord Birkenhead.
sentences.zh: 事实上，柯林斯开始提前一点到达会场，这样他们就能和伯肯黑德勋爵闲聊一会儿。

sentences.en: I love this.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: That's your dream dinner party, right?
sentences.zh: 那是你梦寐以求的晚宴嘉宾，对吧？

sentences.en: Michael Collins and F.E.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·柯林斯和F.E.

sentences.en: Smith.
sentences.zh: 史密斯。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the other person who's really important in this change in the mood, we mentioned him briefly, it's this guy, Tom Jones, this Welshman.
sentences.zh: 那么，在这次情绪转变中另一个非常重要的人，我们刚才简要提过，就是这个叫汤姆·琼斯的威尔士人。

sentences.en: Now, nobody knows about him today, but in the 1920s, he was the ultimate operator.
sentences.zh: 现在没人知道他，但在1920年代，他可是终极操盘手。

sentences.en: One newspaper called him one of the six most powerful people in Europe, which is a big claim.
sentences.zh: 一家报纸称他是欧洲六大权势人物之一，这评价可真高。

sentences.en: I'd love to know who the other five were.
sentences.zh: 我真想知道另外五个人是谁。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: He's working class.
sentences.zh: 他出身工人阶级。

sentences.en: He's also Welsh-speaking.
sentences.zh: 他还会说威尔士语。

sentences.en: He's a former evangelical preacher.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一名福音派传教士。

sentences.en: And he's now become the deputy cabinet secretary, and he is Lloyd George's right-hand man, basically.
sentences.zh: 现在他成了副内阁秘书，基本上是劳合·乔治的得力助手。

sentences.en: Doesn't Lloyd George chat to him in Welsh?
sentences.zh: 劳合·乔治不是会用威尔士语和他聊天吗？

sentences.en: They talk in Welsh in front of other people.
sentences.zh: 他们在别人面前用威尔士语交谈。

sentences.en: Kind of very ostentatiously.
sentences.zh: 显得非常招摇。

sentences.en: Ostentatiously, to annoy.
sentences.zh: 招摇，就是为了惹人厌。

sentences.en: This is another thing that actually I secretly really admire about Lloyd George, because if I could speak Welsh, I would do that all the time.
sentences.zh: 这是我私下里真正佩服劳合·乔治的另一件事，因为如果我会说威尔士语，我也会一直这么做。

sentences.en: So Tom Jones, everybody likes him.
sentences.zh: 所以汤姆·琼斯，大家都喜欢他。

sentences.en: He's very like him.
sentences.zh: 他很讨人喜欢。

sentences.en: And the Irish team really like him, and Lloyd George uses him as a key go-between.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰代表团真的很喜欢他，劳合·乔治把他当作关键的中间人。

sentences.en: And he sends Tom Jones to the Grosvenor Hotel for another of these little meetings with Collins and Griffith.
sentences.zh: 他派汤姆·琼斯去格罗夫纳酒店，与柯林斯和格里菲斯进行另一次这种小会谈。

sentences.en: And Jones says, look, you going on about United Ireland is going to destroy these talks, because the government will never abandon the Ulster Unionists.
sentences.zh: 琼斯说，听着，你们一直纠结爱尔兰统一会毁了这些谈判，因为政府永远不会抛弃阿尔斯特统一派。

sentences.en: But there is an answer, he says.
sentences.zh: 但他又说，不过有一个答案。

sentences.en: There's an answer that could fix this.
sentences.zh: 有一个答案可以解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Now, redrawing borders is all the rage in the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 现在，重划边界在1920年代非常流行。

sentences.en: There has been a big dispute, which is totally forgotten today, but has dominated the headlines all through 1921 between Germany and Poland in Upper Silesia.
sentences.zh: 当时发生了一场大争端，今天已经完全被遗忘了，但在1921年全年都占据了头条，那就是德国和波兰在上西里西亚的争端。

sentences.en: And Jones says, why don't we do what they did in Silesia?
sentences.zh: 琼斯说，为什么我们不效仿他们在西里西亚的做法呢？

sentences.en: They had a boundary commission that drew a new border.
sentences.zh: 他们设立了一个边界委员会来划定新边界。

sentences.en: You know, if we had a boundary commission, I reckon that boundary commission would give you loads of territory.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我们有一个边界委员会，我估计那个委员会会给你们大片领土。

sentences.en: You would get the bits of the six counties that are very Catholic and Tyrone and Fermanagh and stuff.
sentences.zh: 你们会得到六郡中天主教人口众多的部分，还有蒂龙郡和弗马纳郡之类的地区。

sentences.en: Why don't you do that?
sentences.zh: 为什么不这样做呢？

sentences.en: And Griffith says, oh, yeah, that's actually quite a good idea.
sentences.zh: 格里菲斯说，哦，是的，这确实是个好主意。

sentences.en: I love that idea.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个主意。

sentences.en: Who would be on this boundary commission?
sentences.zh: 谁会进入这个边界委员会？

sentences.en: Who would run it?
sentences.zh: 谁来负责？

sentences.en: Well, this is the thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，问题就在这里。

sentences.en: It's not defined.
sentences.zh: 它没有明确定义。

sentences.en: Lloyd George is so cunning with all this.
sentences.zh: 劳合·乔治在这些事情上真是太狡猾了。

sentences.en: I mean, spoiler alert, the boundary commission idea flies, but never really produces anything.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，剧透一下，边界委员会的想法虽然行得通，但从未真正产生任何结果。

sentences.en: And this is because Lloyd George has really thought this through.
sentences.zh: 这是因为劳合·乔治真的深思熟虑过。

sentences.en: And this promise, oh, the boundary commission could give you loads of new territory.
sentences.zh: 这个承诺，哦，边界委员会可能会给你们大片新领土。

sentences.en: It's hanging there.
sentences.zh: 它就悬在那里。

sentences.en: But there is also another possibility.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一种可能性。

sentences.en: The boundary commission could take territory from you.
sentences.zh: 边界委员会也可能从你们那里夺走领土。

sentences.en: And this is never really discussed.
sentences.zh: 而这一点从未真正被讨论过。

sentences.en: Now, when Griffith says, oh, yeah, we could do that.
sentences.zh: 现在，当格里菲斯说，哦，是的，我们可以那样做。

sentences.en: This is a really important moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的时刻。

sentences.en: For the first time, he's going against his instructions from De Valera in Dublin.
sentences.zh: 他第一次违背了都柏林德瓦莱拉给他的指示。

sentences.en: He's using his own initiative, which I think De Valera never expected him to do.
sentences.zh: 他发挥了自己的主动性，我想德瓦莱拉从未预料到他会这样做。

sentences.en: And then the next day, he has a meeting with Lloyd George.
sentences.zh: 第二天，他和劳合·乔治开了一个会。

sentences.en: And Lloyd George is at his most serpentine.
sentences.zh: 劳合·乔治表现得最为阴险。

sentences.en: He says, the Tory press are giving me such a hard time.
sentences.zh: 他说，保守党媒体让我日子很难过。

sentences.en: The Tory diehards.
sentences.zh: 那些保守党的死硬派。

sentences.en: I think my coalition might break up, actually.
sentences.zh: 我想我的联合政府可能真的要解体了。

sentences.en: And I really need your help.
sentences.zh: 我真的需要你们的帮助。

sentences.en: I need to persuade the Ulster Unionists about this boundary commission idea.
sentences.zh: 我需要说服阿尔斯特统一派接受这个边界委员会的想法。

sentences.en: So, please, don't dismiss it publicly.
sentences.zh: 所以，请不要公开拒绝它。

sentences.en: Don't attack it.
sentences.zh: 不要攻击它。

sentences.en: Just pretend that you like it and live with it for the time being.
sentences.zh: 暂时假装你喜欢它并接受它就行。

sentences.en: And Griffith says to him, okay, fine.
sentences.zh: 格里菲斯对他说，好吧，没问题。

sentences.en: I understand.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: You know, I'm not agreeing to it now, but I won't slack it off.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我现在不是同意它，但我不会去诋毁它。

sentences.en: Lloyd George, he says, yeah, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 劳合·乔治说，太棒了。

sentences.en: And the next day, he sends this guy Jones.
sentences.zh: 第二天，他派了那个叫琼斯的人去。

sentences.en: And Jones says, the prime minister has asked me to draw up a document describing yesterday's meeting about the boundary commission.
sentences.zh: 琼斯说，首相让我起草一份文件，描述昨天关于边界委员会的会议。

sentences.en: Do you mind just agreeing to it?
sentences.zh: 你介意同意一下吗？

sentences.en: And Griffith glances at this document and he says, yeah, fine.
sentences.zh: 格里菲斯扫了一眼这份文件，说，好的，没问题。

sentences.en: Looks good.
sentences.zh: 看起来不错。

sentences.en: Looks good.
sentences.zh: 看起来不错。

sentences.en: Now, this is a key moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关键时刻。

sentences.en: When Jones gets back and says, yes, he's fine with it, Lloyd George is delighted.
sentences.zh: 当琼斯回来报告说他同意了，劳合·乔治非常高兴。

sentences.en: And Francis Stevenson says, that night, I have never seen him so excited about anything before.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯·史蒂文森那天晚上说，我从未见过他为任何事情如此兴奋。

sentences.en: And she must have seen him excited about quite a lot of things, I would think.
sentences.zh: 我想她一定见过他为很多事情兴奋过。

sentences.en: She certainly has seen him excited.
sentences.zh: 她当然见过他兴奋。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because this document has done two things.
sentences.zh: 因为这份文件做了两件事。

sentences.en: Number one, Lloyd George has shored up his flank against the Tory diehards.
sentences.zh: 第一，劳合·乔治巩固了自己的侧翼，以抵御保守党死硬派。

sentences.en: He can go to them and say, look, I've persuaded this bloke from Sinn Féin to agree to the boundary commission.
sentences.zh: 他可以去找他们说，看，我已经说服了新芬党的这个家伙同意边界委员会。

sentences.en: So effectively to agree to partition.
sentences.zh: 实际上就是同意了分裂。

sentences.en: But also, he plans to store this document away and to use it against Griffith later, as we shall see.
sentences.zh: 但他也计划把这份文件存起来，以后用来对付格里菲斯，正如我们将要看到的那样。

sentences.en: So the British produce a draft treaty.
sentences.zh: 于是英国人拿出了条约草案。

sentences.en: This is very much along the lines that they'd already discussed.
sentences.zh: 这非常符合他们之前讨论的内容。

sentences.en: Ireland becomes a dominion.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰成为自治领。

sentences.en: Northern Ireland does its own thing.
sentences.zh: 北爱尔兰自行其是。

sentences.en: And there's this boundary commission.
sentences.zh: 还有一个边界委员会。

sentences.en: When the Irish team see this draft treaty, some of them go absolutely ballistic.
sentences.zh: 当爱尔兰代表团看到这份条约草案时，有些人彻底炸锅了。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Ireland's still in the empire?
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰还在帝国之内？

sentences.en: Still under the crown?
sentences.zh: 还在王权之下？

sentences.en: No way are we having this.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不可能接受这个。

sentences.en: But Collins has already begun to change his mind.
sentences.zh: 但柯林斯已经开始改变主意了。

sentences.en: He's been doing loads of reading on the dominions.
sentences.zh: 他读了很多关于自治领的书。

sentences.en: And one thing he realizes, and I think he's quite right, is that being a dominion like Canada or like Australia is not an endpoint.
sentences.zh: 他意识到的一点是，我认为他是对的，那就是成为像加拿大或澳大利亚那样的自治领并不是终点。

sentences.en: It's a process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个过程。

sentences.en: So in other words, he realizes that Canada, for example, is going to become a completely independent country.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他意识到，例如加拿大，最终会成为一个完全独立的国家。

sentences.en: And then it's on a sort of conveyor belt that is leading it inexorably towards that status.
sentences.zh: 它正处于一条不可避免地通向那种地位的传送带上。

sentences.en: And he says, look, that's clearly going to happen to Canada and Australia.
sentences.zh: 他说，看，加拿大和澳大利亚显然会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: So that would happen to us, too, if we get on this conveyor belt.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们踏上这条传送带，我们也会发生同样的情况。

sentences.en: We won't get what we want straight away, but we'll get it eventually.
sentences.zh: 我们不会马上得到我们想要的，但最终会得到。

sentences.en: Delayed gratification.
sentences.zh: 延迟满足。

sentences.en: Delayed gratification.
sentences.zh: 延迟满足。

sentences.en: Now, the Irish team are arguing bitterly about this long into the night, which, of course, means they're knackered the next day when they turn up for the full meetings.
sentences.zh: 现在，爱尔兰代表团为此争论不休，直到深夜，这意味着他们第二天参加全体会议时都精疲力竭了。

sentences.en: And all the time, Lloyd George is piling on the pressure.
sentences.zh: 而劳合·乔治一直在施加压力。

sentences.en: He's saying, come on, we need a decision quickly.
sentences.zh: 他说，来吧，我们需要尽快做出决定。

sentences.en: I don't want to restart the war, but I will if I have to.
sentences.zh: 我不想重启战争，但如果必须的话，我会的。

sentences.en: Hurry up, hurry up.
sentences.zh: 快点，快点。

sentences.en: And he keeps saying to them, you must accept the status of a dominion in the empire and you must accept the king.
sentences.zh: 他一直对他们说，你们必须接受帝国自治领的地位，你们必须接受国王。

sentences.en: And that means the Irish MPs or TDs, as they've become, would have to swear an oath of allegiance to the constitution and to his majesty.
sentences.zh: 这意味着爱尔兰议员或TD（议员），正如他们现在所称的那样，必须宣誓效忠宪法和国王陛下。

sentences.en: And again, it's so Brexit, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这又太像英国脱欧了，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's so Brexit.
sentences.zh: 太像英国脱欧了。

sentences.en: It's exactly like the kind of ideological determination on the part of the hardline Brexit negotiators not to have anything to do with EU frameworks of justice or supervisory
sentences.zh: 这完全就像强硬派脱欧谈判代表那种意识形态上的坚定，不愿与欧盟的司法框架或监督

sentences.en: controls or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 控制或任何类似的东西有任何瓜葛。

sentences.en: And more a point of principle than of politics.
sentences.zh: 这更多是原则问题，而不是政治问题。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: But principle matters.
sentences.zh: 但原则很重要。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, principle matters enormously to people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，原则对人们来说极其重要。

sentences.en: Now, the interesting thing is Lloyd George says, look, if you don't like this, we will smash you.
sentences.zh: 现在，有趣的是劳合·乔治说，听着，如果你们不喜欢这样，我们就会摧毁你们。

sentences.en: We will reintroduce troops and we will kill you all.
sentences.zh: 我们将重新派驻军队，并将你们统统杀光。

sentences.en: Is he bluffing?
sentences.zh: 他在虚张声势吗？

sentences.en: I don't think he is bluffing, actually.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我觉得他不是在虚张声势。

sentences.en: Some historians think he was.
sentences.zh: 有些历史学家认为他是。

sentences.en: But I think, I mean, Lloyd George is a man who was sat there quite happily in government as prime minister during the bloodiest days of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，我是说，劳合·乔治在第一次世界大战最血腥的日子里，一直稳坐政府总理之位，过得相当惬意。

sentences.en: He's perfectly capable of sending thousands of troops to fight and die and to kill in Ireland, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为，他完全有能力派遣成千上万的军队去爱尔兰作战、牺牲并杀戮。

sentences.en: And as we will see, Griffith and Collins both completely believe that he would restart the war if he had to.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将要看到的，格里菲斯和柯林斯都完全相信，如果必须的话，他会重启战争。

sentences.en: So let's move towards the first week in December, which is the deadline that Lloyd George has set.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们进入12月的第一周，这是劳合·乔治设定的最后期限。

sentences.en: So we're on the first Saturday of December, the 3rd.
sentences.zh: 现在是12月的第一个星期六，即3号。

sentences.en: The Irish team are back in Dublin.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰代表团回到了都柏林。

sentences.en: They've gone to meet de Valera and his cabinet.
sentences.zh: 他们去见了德瓦莱拉和他的内阁。

sentences.en: They get there very late.
sentences.zh: 他们到达得很晚。

sentences.en: Their boat collided with a schooner in the Irish Sea.
sentences.zh: 他们的船在爱尔兰海与一艘纵帆船相撞了。

sentences.en: So they're knackered.
sentences.zh: 所以他们累坏了。

sentences.en: That's very riddle of the sands, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这很有《沙之谜》的感觉，不是吗？

sentences.en: Very riddle of the sands.
sentences.zh: 非常有《沙之谜》的感觉。

sentences.en: They've been bickering all the way.
sentences.zh: 他们一路上都在争吵。

sentences.en: Griffith says, look, this is the best we're going to get.
sentences.zh: 格里菲斯说，看，这就是我们能得到的最好结果了。

sentences.en: Everybody wants peace.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想要和平。

sentences.en: We just have to suck up the crown and the empire and the oath.
sentences.zh: 我们只能接受王室、帝国和效忠誓词。

sentences.en: Barton and Gavin Duffy say, no, that's rubbish.
sentences.zh: 巴顿和加文·达菲说，不，那是胡扯。

sentences.en: The British are bluffing.
sentences.zh: 英国人在虚张声势。

sentences.en: They'll never start the war again.
sentences.zh: 他们永远不会再发动战争了。

sentences.en: Collins is a bit ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 柯林斯的态度有点暧昧。

sentences.en: He says, I don't like the oath.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不喜欢那个誓词。

sentences.en: I'm not happy about the deal.
sentences.zh: 我对这份协议并不满意。

sentences.en: But, and I quote, England could arrange a war in Ireland within a week.
sentences.zh: 但是，引用他的话，英国可以在一周内就在爱尔兰安排一场战争。

sentences.en: Like, de Valera, of course, has still not set foot in London during this process, says, listen, I think you should go back to London.
sentences.zh: 就像德瓦莱拉，当然，他在整个过程中从未踏足伦敦，他说，听着，我认为你们应该回到伦敦。

sentences.en: Why don't you try pushing my external association idea again?
sentences.zh: 为什么不试着再次推动我的外部联系构想呢？

sentences.en: You can imagine like, oh, God, come on.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，天哪，拜托。

sentences.en: And he says, crucially, this is really important to explain what happens in the next couple of episodes that we'll do.
sentences.zh: 他关键地说道，这对解释我们接下来几集要讲的内容非常重要。

sentences.en: De Valera says, please keep me and my cabinet in the loop.
sentences.zh: 德瓦莱拉说，请让我和我的内阁随时了解情况。

sentences.en: Do not sign anything without agreeing it with me.
sentences.zh: 在与我达成一致之前，不要签署任何东西。

sentences.en: And Robert Barton at this point says to him, why will you not come with us?
sentences.zh: 而罗伯特·巴顿此时对他说，你为什么不跟我们一起去？

sentences.en: Come with us to London.
sentences.zh: 跟我们一起去伦敦吧。

sentences.en: And de Valera says, no, no, I'm actually fine here.
sentences.zh: 德瓦莱拉说，不，不，我在这里挺好的。

sentences.en: I'm quite happy here.
sentences.zh: 我在这里很开心。

sentences.en: Because it seems to me that what de Valera doesn't want to compromise with more than anything is his own sense of his own virtue.
sentences.zh: 因为在我看来，德瓦莱拉最不愿妥协的，是他对自己美德的自我感觉。

sentences.en: And there's an amazing comment that Ronan Fanning quotes in his book.
sentences.zh: 罗南·范宁在他的书中引用了一个令人惊叹的评论。

sentences.en: And he quotes Lionel Curtis, who is a British official, involved in the negotiations.
sentences.zh: 他引用了参与谈判的英国官员莱昂内尔·柯蒂斯的话。

sentences.en: And Curtis has said of the British, the greatest strength of the British people lies in their inveterate belief that whatever else happens,
sentences.zh: 柯蒂斯曾这样评价英国人：英国人民最大的力量在于他们根深蒂固的信念，即无论发生什么，

sentences.en: they and their leaders will blunder horribly.
sentences.zh: 他们和他们的领导人都会犯下可怕的错误。

sentences.en: And then he says the greatest weakness of the Sinn Féin government is that it is almost void of any admission to the world of themselves that they can either think what is wrong or do what is wrong.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，新芬党政府最大的弱点在于，他们几乎从不向世界或他们自己承认，他们可能会有错误的想法或做出错误的行为。

sentences.en: And that seems to me actually to map very well onto the kind of the governing principles in the negotiations.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这实际上与谈判中的治理原则非常吻合。

sentences.en: And actually, I mean, it also maps on quite well onto the Brexit negotiations as well.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，它与英国脱欧谈判也相当吻合。

sentences.en: Isn't it the difference between one team that's motivated largely by pragmatism?
sentences.zh: 这难道不是一个主要由实用主义驱动的团队与另一个团队之间的区别吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they have no sense that this is a process in which morality plays any part at all.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不认为这是一个道德发挥任何作用的过程。

sentences.en: And another team who genuinely believe that they're on the side of right and virtue and freedom and independence and all of those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 而另一个团队则真诚地相信他们站在正义、美德、自由、独立以及所有这些事物的一边。

sentences.en: So any compromise is going to be very difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以任何妥协都将非常困难。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think that must be a huge part of it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一定是其中很大一部分原因。

sentences.en: Anyway, by the Sunday evening, they're back in London.
sentences.zh: 总之，到了周日晚上，他们回到了伦敦。

sentences.en: That's the 4th of December.
sentences.zh: 那是12月4日。

sentences.en: They go back to Downing Street yet again for about the 5,000th time they have an argument about the partition of Ireland and the oath to the crown.
sentences.zh: 他们又一次回到唐宁街，大概是第5000次了，他们就爱尔兰的分治和对王室的誓词进行了争论。

sentences.en: And Lloyd George now is just in pure kind of performative, melodramatic mood.
sentences.zh: 而劳合·乔治现在完全处于一种表演性的、戏剧化的情绪中。

sentences.en: He kind of says, we're going to have to have a private meeting, me and my team.
sentences.zh: 他大概是说，我们得开个私人会议，我和我的团队。

sentences.en: They go out and they have a private meeting.
sentences.zh: 他们走出去开了个私人会议。

sentences.en: And then he comes back in.
sentences.zh: 然后他又回来了。

sentences.en: I mean, they're probably just going out for a smoke or something.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们可能只是出去抽根烟什么的。

sentences.en: And then they come back in and Lloyd George says to the Irish, listen, if you won't enter the empire, if you won't accept the common bond of the crown,
sentences.zh: 然后他们回来，劳合·乔治对爱尔兰人说，听着，如果你们不加入帝国，如果你们不接受与王室的共同纽带，

sentences.en: then I'm afraid this means war.
sentences.zh: 那么恐怕这意味着战争。

sentences.en: You know, that's how it is.
sentences.zh: 你知道，事实就是这样。

sentences.en: And is he bluffing?
sentences.zh: 他在虚张声势吗？

sentences.en: I don't think he is.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他是。

sentences.en: The next morning, Monday the 5th, his team prepare a draft statement on the collapse of the talks.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上，即5号星期一，他的团队准备了一份关于谈判破裂的草案声明。

sentences.en: They put all the blame on Sinn Féin and they send a coded message to the army in Ireland saying, prepare for hostilities within days.
sentences.zh: 他们把所有责任都推给新芬党，并向爱尔兰的军队发送了一条加密信息，称：准备在几天内开战。

sentences.en: Later that morning, Lloyd George asks to see Collins alone.
sentences.zh: 那天晚些时候，劳合·乔治要求单独见柯林斯。

sentences.en: And they don't decide anything.
sentences.zh: 他们什么也没决定。

sentences.en: But Lloyd George, by doing that, is clearly sending Collins, I think, a message.
sentences.zh: 但劳合·乔治通过这样做，显然是在向柯林斯传递一个信息，我想。

sentences.en: You are a serious person like me.
sentences.zh: 你和我一样是个严肃的人。

sentences.en: Come on, we can fix this.
sentences.zh: 来吧，我们可以解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Help me to fix it.
sentences.zh: 帮我解决它。

sentences.en: Bring the others this afternoon and we'll have one last meeting and we'll have one last go.
sentences.zh: 今天下午把其他人带过来，我们进行最后一次会议，做最后一次尝试。

sentences.en: So that afternoon, three o'clock, the Irish delegates return to Downing Street for this last meeting.
sentences.zh: 于是那天下午三点，爱尔兰代表团回到唐宁街参加最后一次会议。

sentences.en: It's a very tense mood.
sentences.zh: 气氛非常紧张。

sentences.en: This time there are no cheering crowds with flags or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 这次没有欢呼的人群，也没有旗帜之类的东西。

sentences.en: They've run out of money.
sentences.zh: 他们的钱花光了。

sentences.en: So the first time they ever arrived, they arrived in multiple cars.
sentences.zh: 所以他们第一次到达时，是坐着多辆车来的。

sentences.en: This time they all have to cram into one car.
sentences.zh: 这次他们不得不挤进一辆车里。

sentences.en: All sitting on each other's laps.
sentences.zh: 所有人都坐在彼此的膝盖上。

sentences.en: It's a very indecorous arrival.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常不得体的到达方式。

sentences.en: And the British have slimmed down their team.
sentences.zh: 英国人精简了他们的团队。

sentences.en: So there's just four people facing them at the table.
sentences.zh: 所以桌对面只有四个人。

sentences.en: There's Lloyd George.
sentences.zh: 有劳合·乔治。

sentences.en: There is Churchill.
sentences.zh: 有丘吉尔。

sentences.en: There's Lord Birkenhead.
sentences.zh: 有伯肯黑德勋爵。

sentences.en: And there's Austin Chamberlain, the Conservative leader.
sentences.zh: 还有保守党领袖奥斯汀·张伯伦。

sentences.en: Churchill said afterwards, death stood at our elbow.
sentences.zh: 丘吉尔后来曾说，死亡就在我们肘边。

sentences.en: Yeah, because they do think the war could be on tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为他们确实认为明天就可能开战。

sentences.en: And what happens now is the supreme exhibition of Lloyd George's cunning.
sentences.zh: 现在发生的是劳合·乔治狡诈的巅峰展示。

sentences.en: He starts off by talking about this business of partition of Northern Ireland.
sentences.zh: 他首先谈到了北爱尔兰分治这件事。

sentences.en: The Irish say, we hate it.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰人说，我们讨厌它。

sentences.en: If you scrapped it, if you scrapped the Belfast Parliament and gave us Ulster, maybe we'd accept your dominion status.
sentences.zh: 如果你废除它，如果你废除贝尔法斯特议会并把阿尔斯特给我们，也许我们会接受你们的自治领地位。

sentences.en: And at that, Lloyd George pretends to have a massive temper tantrum.
sentences.zh: 听到这话，劳合·乔治假装大发雷霆。

sentences.en: As Barton says, Lloyd George got excited.
sentences.zh: 正如巴顿所说，劳合·乔治激动起来了。

sentences.en: He shook his papers in the air, declared that we were deliberately trying to bring about a break on Ulster because our people in Ireland had refused to come within the empire.
sentences.zh: 他挥舞着手中的文件，宣称我们故意试图在阿尔斯特问题上制造破裂，因为我们在爱尔兰的人民拒绝加入帝国。

sentences.en: And now Lloyd George plays his card.
sentences.zh: 现在劳合·乔治打出了他的底牌。

sentences.en: He points at Griffith and he says, you have lied to me.
sentences.zh: 他指着格里菲斯说，你对我撒谎了。

sentences.en: You've let me down.
sentences.zh: 你让我失望了。

sentences.en: You promised me that you would accept my boundary commission.
sentences.zh: 你答应过我你会接受我的边界委员会。

sentences.en: And he pulls out this piece of paper.
sentences.zh: 他拿出了这张纸。

sentences.en: And it's the document that Griffith had approved without properly reading it a month earlier.
sentences.zh: 这就是格里菲斯一个月前在没有仔细阅读的情况下批准的文件。

sentences.en: And the other Irishmen are shocked.
sentences.zh: 其他爱尔兰人都惊呆了。

sentences.en: What's this?
sentences.zh: 这是什么？

sentences.en: What's all this?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: And nobody is more shocked than Griffith himself.
sentences.zh: 没有人比格里菲斯本人更震惊了。

sentences.en: The blood drains from his features.
sentences.zh: 他面如土色。

sentences.en: He's completely thrown by it.
sentences.zh: 他完全被搞懵了。

sentences.en: There's this dreadful silence.
sentences.zh: 现场一片可怕的寂静。

sentences.en: And then he says, well, I said I wouldn't let you down and I won't.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，好吧，我说过我不会让你失望，我也不会。

sentences.en: I will sign the treaty.
sentences.zh: 我会签署条约。

sentences.en: He crumbles.
sentences.zh: 他崩溃了。

sentences.en: He's like the guy who ticks the box on something on the internet, discovers that he's given away all his money to somebody in Russia or something.
sentences.zh: 他就像那种在网上勾选了某个选项，结果发现自己把所有钱都给了俄罗斯某人的人。

sentences.en: He hasn't read the small print.
sentences.zh: 他没有读细则。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Now, as soon as he says that, Lloyd George is sort of, great.
sentences.zh: 现在，他一这么说，劳合·乔治就一副，太好了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: Well, let's move on to these other little minor things.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们继续讨论这些其他的小问题吧。

sentences.en: The seas, the coast, we'll do a compromise.
sentences.zh: 海洋、海岸，我们会做出妥协。

sentences.en: By the way, you can have your own tariffs.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，你们可以有自己的关税。

sentences.en: We'll let you have that.
sentences.zh: 我们会允许你们这样做。

sentences.en: And he says, why don't you have a new version of the oath that we all like, which Michael Collins has drafted.
sentences.zh: 他说，为什么不采用一个我们都喜欢的新版誓词，由迈克尔·柯林斯起草的那种。

sentences.en: So now it's very complicated.
sentences.zh: 所以现在情况变得非常复杂。

sentences.en: This is pure Brexit negotiation, kind of arcane hair spitting.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是英国脱欧式的谈判，一种深奥的吹毛求疵。

sentences.en: Irish MPs will swear allegiance to the king.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰议员将宣誓效忠国王。

sentences.en: And I quote, in virtue of the common citizenship of Ireland with Great Britain
sentences.zh: 引用如下：凭借爱尔兰与大不列颠的共同公民身份，

sentences.en: and her adherence to and membership of the group of nations forming the British Commonwealth of Nations.
sentences.zh: 以及她对构成大英帝国联邦的国家集团的坚持和成员身份。

sentences.en: So they're kind of still swearing the oath.
sentences.zh: 所以他们某种程度上还是在宣誓。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: After this, they have a break.
sentences.zh: 此后，他们休息了一下。

sentences.en: And Lloyd George says, all right, you need to make up your minds now.
sentences.zh: 劳合·乔治说，好吧，你们现在需要做出决定了。

sentences.en: He says, this is now a matter of peace or war.
sentences.zh: 他说，这现在是和平还是战争的问题。

sentences.en: And by the way, I require that all of you sign.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我要求你们所有人都签字。

sentences.en: It has to be unanimous.
sentences.zh: 必须一致通过。

sentences.en: And now the supreme bit of Lloyd George melodrama.
sentences.zh: 现在是劳合·乔治戏剧表演的巅峰时刻。

sentences.en: He gets that two envelopes and he puts them on the table.
sentences.zh: 他拿出两个信封，放在桌子上。

sentences.en: And he says, this first envelope is a statement that you've accepted the terMs.
sentences.zh: 他说，第一个信封是一份声明，说明你们已经接受了条款。

sentences.en: And he says, the other one is their announcement that the talks have failed.
sentences.zh: 他说，另一个是宣布谈判失败的声明。

sentences.en: And that means, and I quote, war within three days.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，引用他的话，三天内开战。

sentences.en: He says, I have standing ready a special train and a destroyer to take one of these letters to Northern Ireland's Prime Minister, Sir James Craig in BelfaSt.
sentences.zh: 他说，我已经准备好了一列专列和一艘驱逐舰，要把其中一封信送到北爱尔兰总理詹姆斯·克雷格爵士在贝尔法斯特的办公室。

sentences.en: Which of the two letters am I to send?
sentences.zh: 我该送哪一封信？

sentences.en: I want your answer by 10 o'clock tonight.
sentences.zh: 我今晚10点前要得到你们的答复。

sentences.en: He really is a wizard, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他真是一个巫师，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's great stuff.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: It's brilliant performative politics.
sentences.zh: 这是精彩的表演政治。

sentences.en: You know, it's very Hollywood.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这非常像好莱坞。

sentences.en: Lloyd George is great at it.
sentences.zh: 劳合·乔治很擅长这个。

sentences.en: It's like kind of pulling two rabbits out of that.
sentences.zh: 这就像从帽子里变出两只兔子一样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So the Irish go back to Knightsbridge and they are absolutely stunned.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰人回到骑士桥时，完全惊呆了。

sentences.en: Gretchen Freeman describes them being in a state of profound anger, despair and panic.
sentences.zh: 格雷琴·弗里曼形容他们当时处于一种极度愤怒、绝望和恐慌的状态。

sentences.en: Griffith says, fine, I'll sign.
sentences.zh: 格里菲斯说，好吧，我签。

sentences.en: Colin says, I'll sign.
sentences.zh: 柯林斯说，我签。

sentences.en: This guy Duggan says he'll sign.
sentences.zh: 这个叫杜根的家伙说他签。

sentences.en: Barson says, there's no way I'm signing.
sentences.zh: 巴森说，我绝对不会签。

sentences.en: Gavin Duffy says, there's no way.
sentences.zh: 加文·达菲说，没门。

sentences.en: What about Childers?
sentences.zh: 那奇尔德斯呢？

sentences.en: Childers is the secretary.
sentences.zh: 奇尔德斯是秘书。

sentences.en: He doesn't get a signature.
sentences.zh: 他没能签字。

sentences.en: He doesn't get a say, but he's sort of, he's fuming on the margins basically the whole time.
sentences.zh: 他没有发言权，但基本上整个过程中他都在一旁愤愤不平。

sentences.en: He's not in favour.
sentences.zh: 他不赞成。

sentences.en: He's not in favour at all.
sentences.zh: 他一点也不赞成。

sentences.en: Then what follows, there's a huge row, a massive row.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了一场巨大的争吵，一场激烈的争吵。

sentences.en: Barson described it later.
sentences.zh: 巴森后来描述了这件事。

sentences.en: He said that Collins and Griffith called us murderers.
sentences.zh: 他说柯林斯和格里菲斯骂我们是杀人犯。

sentences.en: They stated we'd be hanged from lampposts, that we destroy all they fought for.
sentences.zh: 他们说我们会像罪犯一样被吊死在路灯柱上，说我们摧毁了他们为之奋斗的一切。

sentences.en: Basically, Collins and Griffith wear the other blokes down and they say, fine, we'll sign it.
sentences.zh: 基本上，柯林斯和格里菲斯磨掉了其他人的意志，他们说，好吧，我们签。

sentences.en: So they go back to Downing Street.
sentences.zh: 于是他们回到唐宁街。

sentences.en: They're told they had to be about by 10, but they'd been arguing so long they didn't get there till about 11.
sentences.zh: 他们被告知必须在10点前赶到，但因为争论太久，直到11点左右才到。

sentences.en: When they arrived, the British actually expected that they wouldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 当他们到达时，英国人其实以为他们不会签了。

sentences.en: And so Griffith says, fine, we're all agreed.
sentences.zh: 于是格里菲斯说，好吧，我们都同意了。

sentences.en: We'll sign it.
sentences.zh: 我们签。

sentences.en: Lloyd George and his team are absolutely delighted.
sentences.zh: 劳合·乔治和他的团队欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: There's a bit of faffing around over the small print and at 10 past two in the morning of the 6th of December, they sign the treaty.
sentences.zh: 在细则上又磨蹭了一会儿，12月6日凌晨两点十分，他们签署了条约。

sentences.en: And the Irish delegates go out into the fog.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰代表们走进了雾中。

sentences.en: It's a very foggy day, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，那是一个雾气弥漫的日子。

sentences.en: It's the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 那是20世纪20年代。

sentences.en: It's London.
sentences.zh: 那是伦敦。

sentences.en: There's bound to be loads of fog.
sentences.zh: 肯定会有大雾。

sentences.en: They are silent.
sentences.zh: 他们沉默不语。

sentences.en: They're exhausted.
sentences.zh: 他们精疲力竭。

sentences.en: They don't speak to the press.
sentences.zh: 他们没有接受媒体采访。

sentences.en: They just get straight into their car.
sentences.zh: 他们直接上了车。

sentences.en: All of them piling into this one car.
sentences.zh: 所有人都挤进了这一辆车里。

sentences.en: One of them getting in the boot.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人钻进了后备箱。

sentences.en: And they go home.
sentences.zh: 然后他们回家了。

sentences.en: And a few minutes later, Lord Birkenhead and Churchill come out with these massive cigars, smoking them on the steps of Downing Street.
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，伯肯黑德勋爵和丘吉尔叼着巨大的雪茄，在唐宁街的台阶上抽了起来。

sentences.en: Looking like huge, great capitalist imperialists.
sentences.zh: 看起来就像庞大、伟大的资本主义帝国主义者。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Churchill, it's Churchill, of course, inevitably, who announces the deal to the world.
sentences.zh: 当然，不可避免地，是丘吉尔向全世界宣布了这项协议。

sentences.en: So effectively, what you have is you're going to have two entities on the island of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，你将会在爱尔兰岛上拥有两个实体。

sentences.en: The two entities that are there to this day.
sentences.zh: 这两个实体至今仍然存在。

sentences.en: Northern Ireland with its six counties and the other 26, which become what's then called the Irish Free State, which is a literal translation of the Irish term Seastort Éireann,
sentences.zh: 拥有六个郡的北爱尔兰，以及另外26个郡，它们成为了后来所谓的“爱尔兰自由邦”，这是爱尔兰语“Saorstát Éireann”的直译，

sentences.en: which is a term that de Valera had sometimes used himself to describe the Republic.
sentences.zh: 这也是德瓦莱拉有时用来描述共和国的词。

sentences.en: So in other words, the British have got the deal they always wanted.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，英国人得到了他们一直想要的协议。

sentences.en: And I think there are two obvious winners.
sentences.zh: 我认为有两个明显的赢家。

sentences.en: One is Lloyd George.
sentences.zh: 一个是劳合·乔治。

sentences.en: He's, in inverted commas, solved the Irish question, and he's kept his coalition in power with himself at the top.
sentences.zh: 他用引号里的说法“解决了爱尔兰问题”，并保住了自己的联合政府，让自己稳坐高位。

sentences.en: And the other big winners, of course, are the Ulster Unionists.
sentences.zh: 另一个大赢家当然是阿尔斯特统一派。

sentences.en: They have their six-county, two-thirds Protestant-majority state, which is what they wanted.
sentences.zh: 他们得到了他们想要的那个拥有六个郡、三分之二人口为新教徒的州。

sentences.en: And there are two obvious groups of losers.
sentences.zh: 还有两类明显的输家。

sentences.en: So one of them is Unionists and Protestants in the south of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是爱尔兰南部的统一派和新教徒。

sentences.en: So actually people like Sir Edward Carson, who was the original leader of the Unionists.
sentences.zh: 比如爱德华·卡森爵士，他是统一派最初的领导人。

sentences.en: So they find themselves now in a nationalist, Catholic-dominated Southern Ireland, kind of the Irish Free State, which is the one thing they'd always dreaded.
sentences.zh: 他们现在发现自己身处一个民族主义者占主导、天主教徒占多数的南爱尔兰，也就是爱尔兰自由邦，这正是他们一直以来最恐惧的事情。

sentences.en: And then the really big losers, the half a million Catholics who live in a Protestant-dominated Northern Ireland.
sentences.zh: 而真正的超级输家，是生活在以新教徒为主的北爱尔兰的那五十万天主教徒。

sentences.en: And as we will see in a future series that we'll do on the Troubles, they find themselves treated as second-class citizens in everything from politics to housing.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将在未来关于“动乱”的系列节目中看到的那样，他们发现自己在从政治到住房的方方面面都被当作二等公民对待。

sentences.en: As David Trimble, the Unionist leader in the 1990s, said, it was a cold house for Catholics.
sentences.zh: 正如20世纪90年代的统一派领导人大卫·特林布尔所说，那对天主教徒来说是一个寒冷的家。

sentences.en: Now in Britain, people are delighted by the treaty.
sentences.zh: 现在在英国，人们对该条约感到非常高兴。

sentences.en: Lloyd George, when he briefs his cabinet, he says, I mean, this will surprise, I think, a lot of listeners to this show.
sentences.zh: 劳合·乔治在向内阁通报情况时说，我想这会让很多听众感到惊讶。

sentences.en: He says, this is one of the greatest days in the history of the British Empire.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是大英帝国历史上最伟大的日子之一。

sentences.en: We have fixed this problem and Ireland is still part of our family.
sentences.zh: 我们解决了这个问题，爱尔兰仍然是我们家庭的一部分。

sentences.en: The King sends him a telegram of congratulations.
sentences.zh: 国王给他发来了贺电。

sentences.en: The stock market booms, all his sweetness and light.
sentences.zh: 股市繁荣，一切都显得美好而光明。

sentences.en: But in Dublin, it is a very, very different story.
sentences.zh: 但在都柏林，情况却截然不同。

sentences.en: When de Valera was told the deal had been signed, he said, what?
sentences.zh: 当德瓦莱拉被告知协议已经签署时，他说，什么？

sentences.en: They haven't checked with me.
sentences.zh: 他们没有跟我商量。

sentences.en: They're meant to have checked with me.
sentences.zh: 他们本应该跟我商量的。

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 到底怎么回事？

sentences.en: And someone hands him the text and he can't bring himself to read it.
sentences.zh: 有人把文本递给他，他却不忍心读下去。

sentences.en: He is so appalled.
sentences.zh: 他感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: And the problem with the deal, for him and for his fellow hardliners, is not the partition, I think.
sentences.zh: 对他和他的强硬派同僚来说，这份协议的问题不在于分裂，我认为。

sentences.en: I mean, I think all the Irish historians would agree with this.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我想所有爱尔兰历史学家都会同意这一点。

sentences.en: They don't like partition, but they never really expected they would get the whole island.
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢分裂，但他们从未真正指望能得到整个岛屿。

sentences.en: That ship had sailed.
sentences.zh: 那已经是过去式了。

sentences.en: The real issue is this key issue of principle, which is the oath of allegiance to the British monarch.
sentences.zh: 真正的问题在于这个关键的原则问题，即对英国君主的效忠誓言。

sentences.en: So Michael Collins says, come on, these are just words.
sentences.zh: 所以迈克尔·柯林斯说，得了吧，这只是些文字而已。

sentences.en: Who cares?
sentences.zh: 谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: Doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: But to a lot of Republicans, they say, we're subordinate to the British monarch, really?
sentences.zh: 但对许多共和党人来说，他们会说，我们真的要从属于英国君主吗？

sentences.en: And betraying everything that our comrades fought for?
sentences.zh: 还要背叛我们同志为之奋斗的一切？

sentences.en: The ideal of independence?
sentences.zh: 独立的理想呢？

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 别开玩笑了。

sentences.en: So two days later, the delegates get back and the Irish cabinet meets.
sentences.zh: 两天后，代表们回来，爱尔兰内阁召开了会议。

sentences.en: And the atmosphere is unbelievably toxic.
sentences.zh: 气氛极其恶劣。

sentences.en: De Valera rips into Griffith and Collins.
sentences.zh: 德瓦莱拉猛烈抨击格里菲斯和柯林斯。

sentences.en: You should never have signed this without consulting me.
sentences.zh: 你们根本不该在没咨询我的情况下签署这个协议。

sentences.en: And Griffith snaps back at him.
sentences.zh: 格里菲斯反唇相讥。

sentences.en: He says, you didn't go to London.
sentences.zh: 他说，你没去伦敦。

sentences.en: You refused to come.
sentences.zh: 是你拒绝去的。

sentences.en: And this is the consequence.
sentences.zh: 这就是后果。

sentences.en: Now, the thing is, Griffith had broken his promise.
sentences.zh: 问题是，格里菲斯确实违背了他的承诺。

sentences.en: He had said he wouldn't sign, and he did sign it.
sentences.zh: 他说过他不会签，但他还是签了。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, I think, for me, I think De Valera was deranged to think that he could control the negotiations from Dublin.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，在我看来，德瓦莱拉认为自己能从都柏林遥控谈判，简直是疯了。

sentences.en: Or was he just playing a very, very long game?
sentences.zh: 还是说他只是在下一盘很大的棋？

sentences.en: So, Tom, by a long game, you mean, does he think there will be a civil war, he will lose it, and then he will somehow get back into politics eventually?
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，你说的“下一盘很大的棋”，是指他认为会发生内战，他会输掉内战，然后最终以某种方式重返政坛吗？

sentences.en: I don't think he thinks he'll lose it.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他认为自己会输。

sentences.en: I think maybe he thinks that the negotiations will happen, he will stand on the right side of history, the negotiators will fail, the British will have signed the treaty,
sentences.zh: 我想他可能认为谈判会进行，他会站在历史正确的一边，谈判代表会失败，英国人会签署条约，

sentences.en: and so they won't have any appetite for war, and he can just step in and be the hero.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就不会有战争的胃口，他就可以直接介入并成为英雄。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think he does think that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想他是这么想的。

sentences.en: I think he thinks he will ride in at the end as the hero of the hour, and he has been denied that opportunity because they have signed this treaty.
sentences.zh: 我想他认为他会在最后作为英雄登场，而现在因为他们签署了这份条约，他失去了这个机会。

sentences.en: There'll be some listeners who are more sympathetic to De Valera, who say, you know, he was betrayed by his negotiators or whatever.
sentences.zh: 有些听众可能更同情德瓦莱拉，他们会说，你知道，他被他的谈判代表背叛了之类的。

sentences.en: Ronan Fanning, who's his biographer, accuses him of a gross evasion of the responsibilities of leadership.
sentences.zh: 他的传记作者罗南·范宁指责他严重逃避了领导责任。

sentences.en: And I think, I mean, all this difference between Lloyd George and De Valera is Lloyd George takes personal control of the negotiations, they are his baby from start to finish,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，劳合·乔治和德瓦莱拉之间的所有区别在于，劳合·乔治亲自掌控了谈判，从头到尾都是他的心血，

sentences.en: he runs them masterfully, De Valera washes his hands of them and refuses to get involved.
sentences.zh: 他巧妙地运作了这一切，而德瓦莱拉则对此撒手不管，拒绝参与。

sentences.en: And if you're a leader, you have to get involved, I would say.
sentences.zh: 如果你是领导者，你就必须参与其中，我是这么认为的。

sentences.en: But, just to stick up for De Valera, I mean, had the negotiations been happening in Dublin, then he might have turned up.
sentences.zh: 但是，为德瓦莱拉辩护一下，如果谈判是在都柏林进行的，他可能就会出现了。

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: There is no parallel universe, by the way, in which those negotiations happen in Dublin.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，不存在一个谈判在都柏林进行的平行宇宙。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Anyway, by the end of that day, Irish politics is already irretrievably divided.
sentences.zh: 总之，那一天结束时，爱尔兰政坛已经不可挽回地分裂了。

sentences.en: The cabinet voted by four to three, the Irish cabinet, to back the deal, and De Valera was furious, and he issued a statement straight away.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰内阁以四比三的投票结果支持该协议，德瓦莱拉大发雷霆，并立即发表了一份声明。

sentences.en: He said, the deal is in violent conflict with the wishes of the majority of this nation, which is not actually, as it turns out, true.
sentences.zh: 他说，该协议与本国大多数人的意愿发生剧烈冲突，事实证明，这其实并不是真的。

sentences.en: There's then an incredibly bitter debate in the Doyle, which dragged on into January.
sentences.zh: 随后在爱尔兰议会中进行了一场极其激烈的辩论，一直拖到了1月。

sentences.en: On the one hand, you have the anti-treaty people who say you've betrayed the ideal of the Republic, you've betrayed all our friends who died.
sentences.zh: 一方面，反条约派说你们背叛了共和国的理想，背叛了我们所有牺牲的朋友。

sentences.en: And on the other hand, you have, most famously, Collins.
sentences.zh: 而另一方面，最著名的是柯林斯。

sentences.en: Collins really puts himself on the line defending this.
sentences.zh: 柯林斯为了捍卫这一点，真的把自己豁出去了。

sentences.en: He says, this is the best deal we could get.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是我们能得到的最好的协议。

sentences.en: We're never going to win a war against the British.
sentences.zh: 我们永远不可能打赢一场对英国的战争。

sentences.en: We've made the biggest step towards independence in Ireland's history.
sentences.zh: 我们已经迈出了爱尔兰历史上迈向独立最大的一步。

sentences.en: And he says, it doesn't give us everything we want, but, famous quotation, it gives us the freedom to achieve it.
sentences.zh: 他说，它没有给我们想要的一切，但用那句名言来说，它给了我们实现目标的自由。

sentences.en: The Doyle voted on the 7th of January, and they voted by 64 votes to 57 to back the treaty.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰议会在1月7日进行了投票，以64票对57票支持该条约。

sentences.en: De Valera led his supporters out of the chamber the next day, and Collins shouts at them as they go out, and he calls them deserters.
sentences.zh: 第二天，德瓦莱拉带领他的支持者走出了议会大厅，柯林斯在他们离开时冲他们大喊，称他们为逃兵。

sentences.en: And his parting shot, as De Valera and Erskine Childers go out of the chamber, he goes for the worst insult in the Irish political lexicon.
sentences.zh: 当德瓦莱拉和厄斯金·奇尔德斯走出大厅时，他抛出了最后一句狠话，使用了爱尔兰政治词典中最恶毒的侮辱。

sentences.en: He says, foreigners, Americans, English.
sentences.zh: 他说，外国人，美国人，英国人。

sentences.en: Yeah, because De Valera had been born in America, and Childers, of course, was English.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为德瓦莱拉出生在美国，而奇尔德斯当然是英国人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, in the next few weeks, the Republican movement tears itself apart.
sentences.zh: 所以，在接下来的几周里，共和运动四分五裂。

sentences.en: Even the IRA splits into competing factions.
sentences.zh: 甚至爱尔兰共和军也分裂成了相互竞争的派系。

sentences.en: And on the 14th of April, 1922, about 150 armed IRA fighters, anti-treaty faction, occupy one of the biggest buildings in Dublin, which is the Four Courts Legal Complex.
sentences.zh: 1922年4月14日，大约150名反条约派的武装爱尔兰共和军战士占领了都柏林最大的建筑之一——四法院法律大楼。

sentences.en: And they're doing this as a deliberate provocation to the new pro-treaty government of Griffith and Collins, and, indeed, to the British.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做是对格里菲斯和柯林斯的新亲条约政府，乃至对英国的蓄意挑衅。

sentences.en: For the next few weeks, they are still there in this building, and everybody is waiting, and the tension is rising.
sentences.zh: 接下来的几周，他们一直待在那栋楼里，每个人都在等待，紧张局势不断升级。

sentences.en: And then, on the 22nd of June, news arrives from London of an assassination on the streets of London in broad daylight that shocks the world and will change everything.
sentences.zh: 然后，在6月22日，伦敦传来了消息，伦敦街头发生了一起光天化日之下的暗杀事件，震惊了世界，并将改变一切。
